text:
Maria: Heads up — product wants a new routing knob for latency-aware shard routing so customers can prefer the lowest p99 region for a route but still have deterministic shard affinity for cache locality.
AJ: Do we mean a hybrid policy: latency-first but sticky by shard-key? What's the exact requirement from product?
Maria: Basically: prefer region with lowest observed latency for the route, but when a request contains a shard header we try to keep that shard on the same region unless latency is > X ms. Fallback regions should be an explicit list, not implicit cheapest.
Devon: I recall we already have region_affinity + failover lists, but they don't consider live latency metrics. We'd need a fast routing decision path that reads recent p50/p99 from telemetry, not a heavyweight call.
Samir: We can approximate with a sliding window in the router cache (per route + minute). Keep p50/p99 stats from edge telemetry, update every 30s. Routing decision = prefer region R if p99(R) < threshold OR p50 difference > delta.
Liz: Question: header precedence? Product wants an override header X-Region-Prefer that can pin to a region for compliance. Should that beat latency logic?
AJ: Override headers -> absolute precedence. If X-Region-Prefer present, honor it (and reject if region unavailable). Otherwise apply latency+shard logic.
Maria: Also need to handle quota / plan tiers: enterprise customers can opt-in to preferred-region SLAs. Routing must respect tenant-level locks.
Devon: Edge case: shard affinity + autoscaling/eviction. If a region is overloaded, we should relocate shards gradually. Propose: if region CPU/GPU > 90%, initiate soft-eviction: route new shards to fallback but continue serving existing connections for a TTL.
Samir: Soft-eviction seems right. For deterministic relocation we should set X-Shard-Owner header when we migrate to signal downstream caches.
AJ: Prototype config snippet I sketched:
```
route: /v1/generate
policy:
  mode: latency_sticky
  latency_threshold_ms: 120
  shard_header: X-Shard-Key
  override_header: X-Region-Prefer
  fallback_regions: [us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1]
```
AJ: Router will consult telemetry cache, then compute allowed regions, then pick either pinned shard region (if within threshold) or best latency region.
Liz: Telemetry cache TTL needs tuning. Too long and we route badly during incidents; too short and we thrash. Recommend 30s TTL + exponential backoff on updates when stable.
Maria: Observability: product wants per-route breakdown: chosen_region, reason (latency|shard|override|quota), telemetry_p99_at_decision, and fallback_used boolean. Push these to tracing plus a metrics label region_election.
Devon: Agree. Also emit events when we evict shards or when soft-eviction starts for a tenant. That's important for SRE.
Samir: Security check: header overrides might be abused. Only allow X-Region-Prefer if tenant has permission flag. Otherwise strip header at edge.
AJ: Good call. AuthZ param: allow_region_override: true/false per-tenant. If false -> header dropped and logged.
Liz: UX in console: add per-route toggles: Mode (latency_sticky / shard_only / region_lock), latency_threshold slider, allowed fallbacks, tenant override toggle. Preview panel showing sample decisions given recent telemetry.
Maria: Rollout plan: feature-flag the router behavior behind ff:latency_sticky_v1. Start with internal tenants and a few trusted customers, capture telemetry + decision reasons, run canary 1%->10%->50%.
Devon: Must ensure deterministic decisions in canary: same inputs -> same output. No random tiebreakers; use stable ordering on region id.
Samir: Fail-safes: if telemetry missing or stale -> fallback to static failover list. If routing endpoint fails -> 502 with clear message.
infra-bot: Deploy queued for router-service/latency-policy PR #452 by AJ. Running integration tests (routing deterministic checks).
Maria: Next steps: AJ to open RFC with config schema + API change for X-Region-Prefer & X-Shard-Owner. Devon to draft telemetry labels. Samir to add tenant flag checks. I'll coordinate console mocks with Liz.
AJ: I'll include a sample migration script to backfill current shard_owners into header cache for warmup.
Liz: Thanks. Quick question — do we want to allow composition: latency_sticky + quantile-override per-tenant? Or just global policy?
Maria: Per-route and per-tenant overrides possible but default to route-level config. Keep UX surface limited.
Devon: I'm adding a checklist for SRE runbook: detection of region thrash, rollback ff, forced pinning per-tenant.
Maria: :thumbsup: Thanks team. RFC target EOW.
